text: Trainers' frauds against their own horses
why: The story has just described cases where trainers laid bets against their own horses and then stopped them by fraud, so this name for that practice is already in the text.

text: Cases before now, when trainers laid against their own horses and stopped them by fraud
why: This matches ¶220 almost word for word: 'There have been cases before now where trainers have made sure of great sums of money by laying against their own horses.'

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse?
why: Holmes has raised this motive in ¶220 as the likely explanation for why Straker took the horse out, so it is a plain question the story has given reason to consider.

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse? — yes, through agents
why: The 'through agents' mechanism is stated for the general cases in ¶220, and Holmes now suspects Straker, so 'yes, through agents' is a possibility the reader has reason to consider. It is not confirmed, but the label does not claim it is.

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse? — no: someone else paid him to stop the horse
id: q.straker_bets=no: someone else paid him to stop the horse
why: The story has not raised the idea that someone else paid Straker to stop the horse. Brown's large bets and dislike of Straker hint at a rival's interest, but nothing so far suggests a payment to Straker, so this answer points to a possibility the reader has no reason yet to consider.
